name: The nobles who exacted usury of their brethren
charge: Lending on interest; taking brethren's lands and children for debt
summary: During the rebuilding of the wall, the poor cried out that they had mortgaged their fields and vineyards and sold their sons and daughters into bondage to pay the king's tribute and the nobles' interest. Nehemiah was very angry and set a great assembly against the nobles and rulers.
offense: Families had mortgaged fields, vineyards, and houses for grain and borrowed for the king's tribute. Their children were being brought into bondage, and they lacked the means to redeem them because others held their property. The cry came against their own brethren, not merely against the foreign power taxing them (Nehemiah 5:1-5). Nehemiah rebuked the nobles and rulers for exacting usury. Some Jews were being redeemed from the nations while others were being sold by their own people. The lenders had no answer. Their conduct contradicted the fear of God and exposed the restored community to reproach before its enemies (Nehemiah 5:6-9).
judgment: Nehemiah required immediate restoration of lands, houses, and the hundredth part of the money and produce exacted. The nobles promised to restore and require nothing further. He called the priests and bound the promise by an oath (Nehemiah 5:10-12). Shaking out his lap, he declared that God should likewise shake from house and labor the man who failed to perform it. The congregation answered Amen, praised the Lord, and did according to the promise. Correction reached the possessions taken and the practice that had taken them; a spoken apology alone would not have released the burdened households.

judgmentFull: Nehemiah required immediate restoration of lands, houses, and the hundredth part of the money and produce exacted. The nobles promised to restore and require nothing further. He called the priests and bound the promise by an oath (Nehemiah 5:10-12).

Shaking out his lap, he declared that God should likewise shake from house and labor the man who failed to perform it. The congregation answered Amen, praised the Lord, and did according to the promise. Correction reached the possessions taken and the practice that had taken them; a spoken apology alone would not have released the burdened households.

verses.text: And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.
For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters, are many: therefore we take up corn for them, that we may eat, and live.
Some also there were that said, We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.
There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards.

Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.
And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.
Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.

And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.
Also I said, It is not good that ye do: ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies?
I likewise, and my brethren, and my servants, might exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury.

Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, that ye exact of them.

Then said they, We will restore them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this promise.

Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise, even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation said, Amen, and praised the Lord. And the people did according to this promise.
If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.
And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee.
Take thou no usury of him, or increase: but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee.
Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase.
And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:
But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile:
And then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.
Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God.
Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother; usury of money, usury of victuals, usury of any thing that is lent upon usury:

Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury; but unto thy brother thou shalt not lend upon usury: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all that thou settest thine hand to in the land whither thou goest to possess it.
He that hath not given forth upon usury, neither hath taken any increase, that hath withdrawn his hand from iniquity, hath executed true judgment between man and man,

entries.commentary: There is a great cry of the people and their wives against their brethren the Jews. Even in the middle of the outside threat, a wrong rises up inside the camp among the people themselves.
Some say their sons and daughters are many, and they take up corn for them that they may eat and live. The people are burdened, having to trade for grain simply to keep their large households alive.
Others say they have mortgaged their lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn because of the dearth. The famine forces the people to put up their property just to feed their families.
Still others say they have borrowed money for the king's tribute upon their lands and vineyards. The heavy tax drives the people into debt against the very land they depend on.

Their flesh is as the flesh of their brethren, yet they are bringing their sons and daughters into bondage, and some daughters are already brought to bondage with no power to redeem them. Their own brethren are enslaving them over debt though they are one flesh, one people just come out of captivity.
When Nehemiah hears their cry and these words he is very angry. The oppression of the people by their own brethren stirs his anger.

Nehemiah consults with himself, rebukes the nobles and rulers for exacting usury each from his brother, and sets a great assembly against them. He brings a great multitude before the nobles to make the point plain that lending against their brethren for gain is usury and wrong.

Nehemiah reminds them that he and his have redeemed their brethren the Jews from the heathen, and asks if they will now sell their own brethren, so that they hold their peace and find nothing to answer. The nobles are silenced because they have no answer for enslaving the same brothers others labored to buy back from the heathen.

Nehemiah says it is not good what they do, and asks if they ought not to walk in the fear of God because of the reproach of the heathen their enemies. Their conduct toward their brethren should be governed by the fear of the Most High, especially with the enemies watching.

Nehemiah says he, his brethren, and his servants might also exact money and corn, but pleads that they leave off this usury. Even those with the right to lend are called to give up usury against their own people.

Nehemiah asks them to restore that same day the lands, vineyards, oliveyards, and houses, and the hundredth part of the money, corn, wine, and oil they had exacted. He calls for full and immediate restoration of what was taken from the brethren.

They agree to restore everything and require nothing, so Nehemiah calls the priests and takes an oath of them to do according to this promise. The promise is bound by oath before the priests so it cannot be quietly abandoned.

Nehemiah shakes his lap and says so may the Most High shake out every man from his house and labor who does not perform this promise, and all the congregation says Amen and praises the Lord, and the people do according to the promise. A visible sign seals the oath, and the whole congregation agrees, and the people keep the promise.

From the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, twelve years as governor in Judah, Nehemiah and his brethren do not eat the bread of the governor. Nehemiah refuses the provision owed to his office, governing for twelve years without taking from the people.

The former governors were chargeable to the people, taking bread, wine, and forty shekels of silver, and their servants bore rule over the people, but Nehemiah does not do so because of the fear of God. The fear of the Most High keeps Nehemiah from the burden and rule that earlier governors laid on the people.
Nehemiah continues in the work of the wall, buys no land, and gathers all his servants to the work. He gives himself and his household to the labor rather than to gaining property.

Daily one ox, six choice sheep, and fowls are prepared for him, with store of wine every ten days, yet he does not require the bread of the governor because the bondage was heavy upon the people. Though he provides a table, he refuses to charge the people for it, sparing them because their burden is already heavy.

Nehemiah asks the Most High to think upon him for good according to all he has done for the people. Nehemiah was about the work and for the people, not the usery of the people, and he commits his labor to the remembrance of the Most High.

If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

When ye come into the land which I give you, six years thou shalt sow thy field and prune thy vineyard, but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the Lord: no sowing, no pruning, no reaping of that which groweth of its own accord. As we rest on the seventh day, the land rests the seventh year. Letting the land rest is harmony and balance on the earth, and the sabbath of the land is meat for thee, thy servants, the stranger, thy cattle, and the beasts in thy land. These land laws were given for the land of Israel; land bought in this captivity is not under the seventh year rest.

Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, forty and nine years; then shall thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement, throughout all your land. Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you, and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and every man unto his family. Neither sow, nor reap that which groweth of itself, for it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you.

If thou sell ought unto thy neighbour, or buyest ought of thy neighbour's hand, ye shall not oppress one another: according to the number of years after the jubile thou shalt buy, and according unto the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price, for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee. Thou shalt fear thy God, for I am the Lord your God; the price was reckoned honestly to the jubile so no man was oppressed.

Wherefore ye shall do my statutes and keep my judgments, and ye shall dwell in the land in safety, and the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill. If ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow nor gather in our increase: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years. The Most High answered the lack before it came: the sixth year would bring forth enough until the harvests of the ninth year came in, and ye shall sow the eighth year and eat yet of old fruit.

The land shall not be sold for ever, for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Israel was not able to sell away any of the land for ever, because it is the holy land of the Most High, and in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land. If thy brother be waxen poor and hath sold away some of his possession, and any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold; or if the man himself be able, he may redeem it, or it goes out in the jubile and he returns to his possession. Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it meaning to buy it back. This is the prime example to reference for the curse that says no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem you. The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom; Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that.

If a man sell a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold; if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, the house in the walled city is established for ever to him that bought it. But the houses of the villages which have no wall are counted as the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they go out in the jubile. Notwithstanding, the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel. Levi was not given any land; his portion was the offerings of the Lord, and the fields of the suburbs of their cities are their perpetual possession and may not be sold.

If thy brother be waxen poor and fallen in decay with thee, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee. The word stranger does not always mean a heathen; sometimes it is your own brother sojourning away from his land, and the context of the verse tells you which. Thy brother is thy neighbour and the children of thy people: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Brother, neighbour, and children of thy people all mean the same thing. Take thou no usury of him, or increase, but fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee. Usury is interest, a fee accumulating over time; thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase. Lending for the opportunity to make a profit off your own people is evil. I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan. The Most High is not the God of everybody: to bring Israel out He judged Egypt, and to give Israel Canaan He cast out the seven nations, greater and mightier than Israel, delivered them before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period.

If thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor and be sold unto thee, thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant and as a sojourner he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile; then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family and unto the possession of his fathers. The Hebrew servant serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free for nothing; if he came in by himself he goes out by himself, and if he were married his wife goes out with him. That seventh year of release is that servant's jubile: a servant taken in 2012 goes out free in 2019, and one taken in 2019 goes out free in 2026. For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour, but shalt fear thy God; deal with him properly, for the Most High judges both the poor man and the one he serves.

Both thy bondmen and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids, and of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, and they shall be your possession. Ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever. But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

If a sojourner or stranger wax rich by thee, and thy brother that dwelleth by him wax poor and sell himself unto the stranger, after that he is sold he may be redeemed again: one of his brethren may redeem him, either his uncle, or his uncle's son, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family; or if he be able, he may redeem himself, working as an hired servant and earning the price of his own freedom. Here again redeem means buy, as in buying a man out of slavery back to the position of freedom; and the price of his redemption was reckoned with him that bought him, according to the number of years from the year he was sold unto the year of jubile, as the time of an hired servant. If he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he and his children with him. For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. Everybody is not the servant of the Most High; the children of Israel are His servants, and this teaching identifies them today as the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

The word of the Most High asks what they mean by the proverb, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge. As the Most High lives, they shall no more use this proverb in Israel, for all souls are His; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is His. The soul that sinneth, it shall die, setting the theme of individual accountability.

If a man be just and do that which is lawful and right, has not eaten upon the mountains nor lifted his eyes to idols, nor defiled his neighbour's wife, nor oppressed any, but restored the debtor his pledge and given his bread to the hungry, he is just and shall surely live. He has not given forth upon usury nor taken increase, has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, executed true judgment between man and man, and walked in the Most High's statutes.

If that just man beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, who eats upon the mountains, defiles his neighbour's wife, oppresses the poor and needy, spoils by violence, and lifts his eyes to idols, committing abomination. Such a son who gives forth upon usury and takes increase shall not live; he has done all these abominations and shall surely die, and his blood shall be upon him.

If that wicked man beget a son that sees all his father's sins, considers, and does not do likewise, but gives his bread to the hungry, covers the naked, takes off his hand from the poor, and keeps the Most High's judgments and statutes. That son shall not die for the iniquity of his father; he shall surely live, but the father, because he cruelly oppressed and spoiled his brother, shall die in his own iniquity.

They ask why the son does not bear the iniquity of the father, when the son has done that which is lawful and right and kept the statutes; he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die; the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, nor the father the iniquity of the son; the righteousness of the righteous is upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked upon him.

If the wicked turn from all his sins, keep all the Most High's statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live and not die; his transgressions shall not be mentioned unto him. The Most High has no pleasure that the wicked should die, but that he return from his ways and live; yet if the righteous turn away from his righteousness and commit iniquity, all his righteousness shall not be mentioned, and he shall die in his sin.

Yet the house of Israel says the way of the Lord is not equal; the Most High answers, Are not your ways unequal. When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and dies in his iniquity, it is for the iniquity he has done; when a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.

Therefore the Most High will judge the house of Israel, everyone according to his ways; repent and turn yourselves from all your transgressions, so iniquity shall not be your ruin. Cast away all your transgressions and make you a new heart and a new spirit, the heart being the mind, for the Most High has no pleasure in the death of him that dies; wherefore turn yourselves and live. This reading taught repentance, how our enemies take the chief of our young men and women to leave the nation base, and that the Most High has a plan to use the lowly and base to confound the wise, so let your light shine rather than look for any slither of hope to unite with our oppressors. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

lawsResolved.text: If you lend to any of your brethren in need, you are not to take or lay usury upon them.
If one of your brethren becomes poor, you shall exact no usury or interest from him; you shall not lend him your money for usury, nor lend him your food at a profit.
Usury and the usurer are condemned.
You shall not oppress the poor.
Your own brethren are not to be compelled to serve as a slave but shall be treated as a hired servant.
A personal trespass that results in a loss of property is to be repaid in the principal amount plus an additional fifth part added to it.

text.text: And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.
For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters, are many: therefore we take up corn for them, that we may eat, and live.
Some also there were that said, We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.
There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards.

Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.
And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.
Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.

And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.
Also I said, It is not good that ye do: ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies?
I likewise, and my brethren, and my servants, might exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury.

Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, that ye exact of them.

Then said they, We will restore them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this promise.

Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise, even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation said, Amen, and praised the Lord. And the people did according to this promise.
If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury.
And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee.
Take thou no usury of him, or increase: but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee.
Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase.
And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:
But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile:
And then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.
Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God.
Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother; usury of money, usury of victuals, usury of any thing that is lent upon usury:

Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury; but unto thy brother thou shalt not lend upon usury: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all that thou settest thine hand to in the land whither thou goest to possess it.
He that hath not given forth upon usury, neither hath taken any increase, that hath withdrawn his hand from iniquity, hath executed true judgment between man and man,
